_doc: RESILIENCE-1 (Rowan, 2026-11-17): a clock that stops must be rewound by the system, not noticed by a person. Ultrastable is built to keep ticking: every clock (doctrine/clocks.json, plus every scheduled workflow, whose interval is derived from its own cron) has a liveness probe, stall detection and a restart route; every watcher is itself watched by another independent watcher; a restart that does not take is escalated through the queue (Q-STALL-*), never by email. Read by foundation/resilience.py; checked by `python3 -m foundation resilience --check`; the stalled-clock count is the essential variable `stalled_clocks` in doctrine/ultrastability.json, so a stall becomes an Ashby second-order event. Never raise a bound or drop a route to clear a stall.

tick-heartbeat.why: POST /pulse/watch runs a tick only when the newest one is older than two intervals; safe to call by anyone, and each account's Worker is an independent route

criticality-loop.why: the criticality tick runs inside the same Worker tick, so waking the tick restarts it

unlearn-beat.why: POST /pulse/watch runs the Unlearn beat only when the last one is over two hours old; safe to call by anyone; the custom domain and workers.dev are separate routes to the same Worker

what-works-beat.why: POST /pulse/watch runs the What Works beat only when the last one is over two hours old; safe to call by anyone; the custom domain and workers.dev are separate routes to the same Worker

replication-ledger-beat.why: POST /pulse/watch runs the Replication Ledger beat only when the last one is over two hours old; safe to call by anyone; a page visit sparks the same beat as a second route

base-rates-beat.why: POST /pulse/watch runs the Base Rates beat when the last one is over two intervals old; safe to call by anyone; the custom domain and workers.dev are separate routes to the same Worker

open-questions-beat.why: POST /pulse/watch runs the Open Questions beat when the last one is over two intervals old; safe to call by anyone; the custom domain and workers.dev are separate routes to the same Worker

watchers.what: the GitHub Actions watchdog (.github/workflows/watchdog.yml): measures every clock, restarts what stopped
the tick Worker's watchdog loop (seed/worker/src/watchdog.js): dispatches watchdog.yml when its last run is older than two intervals, and beats every tick
the site Worker's hourly watchTick: wakes the tick through the TICK binding when it is stale

site_probes.why: a 503 on the tenant site is answered by redeploying it from its own workflow (LINK-LIVE-1: the same URL is the live link probe)
